questions.question: A context is created with `isMobile: true` and nothing else. What happens when a test calls `locator.tap()`?
options: The tap works, because `isMobile` enables touch
Playwright falls back to a normal click
It fails, because the context also needs `hasTouch: true`
The tap is ignored without an error
questions.explanation: `isMobile` and `hasTouch` are separate options. Without `hasTouch`, `tap()` fails and tells you to enable touch support.

questions.question: A menu opens from a `touchend` listener and has no `click` listener. Which call opens it on a phone preset?
questions.explanation: `tap()` sends `touchstart` and `touchend`. `click()` and `dragTo()` only send mouse events, so a touch-only listener never runs.

questions.question: Why does `test.use({ ...devices['iPhone 15'] })` fail inside a `test.describe()` block?
options: Device presets only work in the config file
`test.use()` is never allowed in a describe block
The preset sets `defaultBrowserType`, and changing the engine forces a new worker
questions.explanation: Move the preset to the top of the file or into a project. Options such as `viewport` are still allowed in a describe block.

questions.question: You want a Pixel 5 test to run in landscape. Which approach changes the page's layout?
options: Swap the width and height in the `screen` option
questions.explanation: The landscape preset sets a landscape viewport. Changing only `screen` leaves the viewport, and so the layout, in portrait.

questions.question: Which context option correctly lets a page read an emulated location?
questions.explanation: The location and the permission are both required, and `permissions` must be an array of permissions to grant.
